title: Chronos few-shot cold-start series identity View
hypothesis: On series identities excluded entirely from shared-code training, one frozen Chronos-T5-Tiny plus a single shared rank-2 lm_head LoRA basis and one few-shot series coordinate m_s can improve future-horizon MASE over zero-shot and pooled LoRA by at least 2%, while using under 10% of the per-series rank-2 LoRA payload. A per-series two-coefficient direct residual and independent rank-2 adapters establish how much private state is needed.
physical_object: One frozen official amazon/chronos-t5-tiny checkpoint and a rank-1 output-logit LoRA basis shared across series.
mirror_coordinate: One scalar angle m_s per series, inferred by minimizing teacher-forced support token NLL on six short forecast windows; it rotates a shared rank-2 LoRA latent. A direct two-coefficient update is the private-coordinate control; no support-selected fallback behavior is claimed.
logical_multiplicity: Few-shot adaptive forecasters for held-out traffic sensor series from one physical Chronos model and one shared LoRA basis.

model.updates: No base-model updates; shared rank-1 LoRA training on fit sensors only, then per-series support adaptation.

data.selection_rule: Freeze the explicit stored sensor ID lists above before accessing their values. Fail/NOT ESTABLISHED if an ID is absent or any series has non-finite values.
data.episode: For each sensor, the first 60% chronological target range supplies six support windows spaced across the range; the final 20% supplies three chronological non-overlapping query windows. Context is 288 steps; each query horizon is 12 steps. Development sensors choose rank/regularization/update count and private-state gate; audit query labels are never used for adaptation or fallback selection.
data.normalization: No validation/test statistics. Chronos native context scaling; MASE lag-1 denominator is calculated from the first 60% prefix only. Also report persistence; seasonal-naive is allowed only when all compared methods have ≥288 context observations.
data.audit_series_rule_amendment: Before the audit protocol was frozen, an exploratory pandas load checked only finiteness of stored sensor positions 22–61; this exposed no target metrics but did touch finite/nonfinite state for proposed IDs 46–61. Those IDs are excluded entirely. Audit is reset to IDs 62–77, which were not read or inspected. All future phase-specific loading uses HDF column hyperslabs, never whole-frame reads.

controls: Pooled rank-2 lm_head LoRA shared across all series, no series code
Shared rank-2 LoRA basis plus learned one-scalar per-series Mirror coordinate m_s
Byte-near per-series diagonal gain on the same shared LoRA feature
Per-series independent rank-2 lm_head LoRA fit with identical six support windows (upper control)
Optional one-scalar private residual rule, selected using two support-only folds under a dev-frozen threshold

development.selection_metric: macro MASE on development future query windows; tie-break on serialized adaptation payload bytes
allowed_changes: LoRA rank from [1,2] on fit/dev only
private residual gate threshold from dev support folds only

metrics.primary: per-series MASE, macro and worst quartile
secondary: CPU fit wall time and query latency

paid_objects: shared LoRA A/B factors and any scaling
series ID map and decoder metadata
any task normalization state required at inference

success_gate: On audit series, Mirror improves macro MASE ≥2% over both Chronos zero-shot and pooled LoRA, is within 5% of independent per-series rank-2 LoRA, uses <10% of independent adaptation bytes, and beats same-cost diagonal-gain control by >0.1%; all serialized replay checks pass.
failure_gate: Mirror misses any quality/storage gate, a same-cost ordinary diagonal gain matches it within 0.1%, or per-series full/independent controls show that one-dimensional m lacks needed functional freedom.
not_established_gate: Pinned model/data inaccessible, API cannot support deterministically trainable shared rank-1 lm_head adapter and exact inference, or required per-series control cannot be reproduced.
boundaries: PEMS-BAY is one network and same timestamp range as MA-1057, though sensor IDs are disjoint; not an independent dataset family.
Chronos pretraining overlap with PEMS-BAY is unknown.
Sensor IDs are held out as complete series from adapter-basis training; support observations on each audit series are allowed only for few-shot adaptation.
No capacity claim from logical combinations; report task quality, bytes and runtime.
MA-1058 tests series identity adaptation, not the mixed-rate calibration tested in MA-1057.
A full two-coefficient per-series update is treated as the private-coordinate boundary control; no conditional fallback-selection policy is tested.

amendments.timing: Before model fitting, development metrics, and audit freeze
amendments.reason: Exploratory finite-value screening accidentally inspected finite flags for proposed audit sensor IDs 46–61.
amendments.change: Discard IDs 46–61 and use audit IDs 62–77, never inspected previously. Keep fit 22–37 and dev 38–45. Implement column-selective HDF access.
amendments.impact: No forecasts, target errors, or benchmark metrics were computed for discarded audit sensors. They remain unused. The audit set is unaccessed.
